h1: Quantum Core — AI & SaaS Landing Page Design
tagline: “Talk with the team” — the whole landing page is composed around that line, down to the animation timings.
summary: Landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product — cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) easing, looping video, a stats row and 700ms transitions.
about: Quantum Core shows one way to build the landing page for an AI or SaaS product, and publishes the instructions that produced it. The headline reads “Talk with the team”, and the rest of the landing page is arranged around it. The palette is deep blue #080A19 underneath and white #E9E9E9 for the type, set in Suisse Intl. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 1920x1420 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. Motion is confined to 700ms transitions, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) and a looping video bed. Keep it open while you write: the 27,320-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: The nav is deliberately thin
layout.body: The wordmark holds the left edge and the links run to the right of it, all of it set in Suisse Intl so the bar belongs to the page below rather than to a separate system. The bar sits over the 1920x1420 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: Sizes fixed in the brief
layout.body: The list stays short (type from 12px to 72px, 20px spacing steps, 700ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) easing), which is why the whole system can be checked by hand. Each value maps to one job: a type step, a gap, a radius or a transition.

layout.title: One row, no drawers
layout.body: One action per bar. The reference was captured at 1920x1420.

layout.title: The spacing steps are quoted
layout.body: Spacing is quoted the same way (type from 12px to 72px, 20px spacing steps, 700ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) easing), not as a scale that grows on its own.

motion.title: A loop, not a timeline
motion.body: One 6.8s clip is the entire ambient layer: it plays behind the copy, loops without a visible cut and never reacts to the pointer. The clip is short enough to loop without a visible seam, which matters more than its resolution.

motion.title: A small interactive surface
motion.body: Every interactive element does one thing (hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card), which is what keeps the states predictable. The states are drawn from the page's own palette rather than from a component default. Keep the interactive layer small.

editorial.title: Making the landing page yours
editorial.body: Suppose you only have one afternoon. Change the headline and the action label, leave type from 12px to 72px and 20px spacing steps alone, and you have a page that looks intentional. Your accent has to survive the same contrast test as the reference accent.

editorial.title: Reading Quantum Core as a spec
editorial.body: The cost of a fixed scale is less room to improvise. type from 12px to 72px and 20px spacing steps keep the composition coherent, but a new element has to be fitted rather than placed. Nothing in this landing page depends on a default.

editorial.title: What this landing page gets right
editorial.body: A stock hero and this landing page use the same parts. Here they are ordered by navigation, the headline, the announcement badge, the stats row and the card grid and measured with type from 12px to 72px, 20px spacing steps, 700ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) easing, so the screen reads as a sequence rather than a container. Quantum Core states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

faq.question: What does the brief behind Quantum Core actually contain?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 27,320 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: How much of Quantum Core depends on React and Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: Quantum Core was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: What drives the motion in Quantum Core?
faq.answer: Entrances and state changes are in the 700ms range on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1). They are driven by state changes rather than a scroll library, and they never hold up the copy.
